- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤-1.0) within 3–5 days, model often fails to correct downward; apply downward bias of 3–7% to next 3–5 periods.
- Model frequently overshoots after strong upward sentiment spikes; cap forecast at 1.5x recent high if sentiment >0.8 for 3+ days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show price decline, model often undercorrects; add 2–5% upward bias to next 2–4 periods.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates late-period prices (last 7–10 days); reduce final 5–7 days by 3–8% if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing midpoint (e.g., if sentiment shifts from +1 to -1, forecast should drop 5–10% in next 3 days).
